response.sql: WITH a AS (SELECT AlbumId, CAST(SUM(Bytes) AS REAL) / SUM(CASE WHEN Bytes IS NOT NULL THEN Milliseconds END) AS rate, COUNT(*) AS n FROM Track GROUP BY AlbumId), m AS (SELECT AVG(rate) AS mean_rate FROM a) SELECT AVG(a.rate) AS avg_rate, AVG(a.n * 1.0) AS avg_track_count, AVG(a.rate - m.mean_rate) AS avg_excess_over_mean FROM a CROSS JOIN m WHERE a.rate > m.mean_rate

assumptions.assumption: An album's rate is total Bytes divided by total Milliseconds, counting only tracks that have a Bytes value in both sums. Albums with no known sizes have a NULL rate, so they are left out of the mean and the above-mean set.
Track count is every track on the album, including tracks with missing Bytes.
Tracks with a NULL AlbumId form a single group, which GROUP BY does by default.
The 'how far above the mean' figure is the average of (album rate minus the overall mean rate) across the above-mean albums.

alternatives.interpretation: An album's rate is the average of each track's own Bytes/Milliseconds ratio, rather than total Bytes over total Milliseconds. Tracks with NULL Bytes are skipped for the rate but still counted as tracks.
